London, 14<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The federal government** will buy about 17,600 fuel-efficient vehicles from the Detroit 3 by June 1, including 2,500 hybrid sedans by April 15.  The purchases for the federal fleet will use $285 million of the $300 million that Congress appropriated in its economic recovery act to buy new vehicles with better fuel economy.  Though the recovery act did not say the purchases had to be from the Detroit 3, the purchases will be from GM, Chrysler and Ford.  Each new vehicle will have better fuel economy than the one it replaces. The federal fleet purchase, the largest in history, will reduce gasoline consumption by 1.3 million gallons a year.  The government will use the remaining $15 million of the recovery act funds for pilot programs using all-electric vehicles and natural-gas and hybrid buses. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Ford had its corporate credit rating** raised by Standard & Poor’s, but the agency remains concerned about Ford’s cash flow in the coming months.   S& P viewed Ford’s reduction of its debt last week to $15.9 billion from $25.8 billion as a “distressed debt exchange,” which equals a default under its criteria. So on April 6, it lowered Ford’s corporate credit rating from CC - 10 steps below investment grade- to its lowest rating, default.  But today S&P said that it raised the rating to CCC+, seven steps below investment grade. The rating improved because the debt reduction, which involved swapping company stock and cash, “improved Ford’s capital structure”.  On Friday, S&P cut GM’s and Chrysler’s corporate credit ratings to CC, one step above the agency’s bankruptcy rating of C. The move indicates concerns that the companies will declare bankruptcy in “coming months or even sooner, in the case of Chrysler”. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**While Germany’s car-scrapping plan** has spurred 1.2 million people to trade in clunkers and buy new, many of the popular models are made abroad. “The scrappage incentive is fanning sales in Eastern Europe and Asia, where the bulk of thrifty, smaller vehicles are made,” said Justus Haucap, economics prof. at Nuremberg University.  “As for Germany, we’re more renowned for our fancy cars and sports vehicles… 2,500 euros gives little or no reason to buy a premium brand like Audi, Mercedes or BMW.” _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Toshiba Corp** is ready to mass-produce a quick-charging lithium ion battery for hybrid vehicles with the highest electrical output for a battery of this kind, said the Nikkei.  Toshiba has quadrupled the output density of its Super Charge ion Battery, or SCiB, to 3,900 watts. Output density is the power output per kilogram of the battery’s weight. The battery can be charged in 90 seconds, and can be recharged over 10,000 times.  Toshiba has started shipping the battery to major Japanese, U.S. and European automakers on a trial basis. It has also developed a lithium ion battery with a high energy densit

y aimed at electric vehicles that will be able to discharge power over a long duration and hopes to start sample shipments in the fall. Toshiba now makes 150,000 SCiBs/month but plans to start building a plant this fall that would make about 2 million batteries a month on start-up, with hopes for expansion to about 10 million by about 2015. _Source: Reuters_ 

**Platinum Australia** said its new mineral resource estimate at the Kalahari Platinum project rose 160 % with the overall grade up almost 2%.  Total contained 3E (platinum, palladium, gold) ounces in the Crater deposit rose to 1.77oz from 0.68Moz; overall grade increased to about 2.04g/tonne 3E PGM. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Absa Capital** (South Africa)plans to launch an exchange traded note on the JSE in H209 to give investors exposure to platinum’s spot price.  It is unclear whether the note will be backed by physical platinum. _Source:  Mining Weekly_
